such as a raging river or a torrent. It emphasizes the force, speed, and

unstoppable force and volume, such as a "torrent of words," a "rushing

Loitering; dawdling; stopping along the way.Nuance:"道草"
 literally means "roadside grass." The idiom "道草を食う" (to eat the 
roadside grass) means to dawdle or waste time on a journey by stopping 
for non-essential reasons, thus being delayed in reaching one's 
destination. The nuance is one of leisurely distraction or time-wasting,
 often without a serious purpose. It can be used neutrally for a 
pleasant detour, but it often carries a mild criticism for causing an 
unnecessary delay. It implies being sidetracked by minor attractions.Example Sentences:家に帰る途中で道草を食って、母に怒られた。I dawdled on my way home and got scolded by my mother.道草を食わずに、まっすぐ帰りなさい。Don't loiter; come straight home.彼は道草を食いながら、ゆっくりと散歩した。He took a slow walk, stopping here and there along the way
